basic_information.short_title: Expanded Special Geographic Area Development Authority
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF AUTHORITY AND SERVICES OF THE SPECIAL GEOGRAPHIC AREA DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 13, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “BANGSAMORO ADMINISTRATIVE CODE”, AND BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 49, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “BANGSAMORO LOCAL GOVERNANCE CODE OF 2023”, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
basic_information.approved_by: Not shown. The approval block of the published copy reads “XXX”.
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days following completion of publication in at least 2 newspapers of regional circulation within the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Puts the Special Geographic Area Development Authority (SGADA) — the body for the 8 municipalities of the Special Geographic Area — on a permanent footing, with a governing Board, an Administrator, defined area-wide services, and a fixed 2.5% of all Bangsamoro Government revenue collections every year.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Section 1 treats the Special Geographic Area as a special development and administrative area, so that services affecting it are planned, supervised and coordinated efficiently. The interim SGADA set up under the Bangsamoro Administrative Code is replaced by an expanded one.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: SGADA takes on services that cross town boundaries or cost too much for any single municipality: development planning; flood control, drainage, sewerage and irrigation; zoning, land use and shelter; health, sanitation and pollution control; public safety and disaster response; and anything else the Chief Minister delegates pursuant to a law. It is not a political subdivision and may not exercise powers reserved to LGUs.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of the 8 Special Geographic Area municipalities
Mayors and councils of those municipalities
Bangsamoro ministries, offices and agencies working in the area
The regional treasury, which carries a standing 2.5% revenue share
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: 15 days after publication is completed in at least 2 newspapers of regional circulation. Passed 16 July 2026; the published copy shows no Chief Minister approval date.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: PASSED 16 JULY 2026. If you live in the Special Geographic Area, one authority now plans and can deliver area-wide services — flood control, land use, health and sanitation, disaster response — funded by 2.5% of all regional revenue every year.
in_practice: SGADA is a special administrative and development authority, not a political subdivision
It plans, monitors and coordinates, and regulates only where the act expressly says so

An SGA Board governs it: a Chairperson appointed by the Chief Minister, 3 ministers or heads of BARMM offices, the President of the SGA League of Mayors, and any additional LGU or private-sector members
An Administrator heads day-to-day operations and appoints staff at Salary Grade 24 and below
Funding: the annual Bangsamoro budget plus a fixed 2.5% of all Bangsamoro Government revenue collections, reviewed by Parliament every 3 years
SGADA may impose fees and charges in accordance with law
It may deliver basic services in a municipality only with that LGU's prior coordination and consent
Interim SGADA staff keep their posts and pay until notified; displaced staff get 1¼ months' salary per year of service
If the area becomes a province or political subdivision, SGADA is phased out within 2 years

for_specific_groups.Residents of the Special Geographic Area: Flood control, drainage, sewerage and irrigation, land use and shelter, health and sanitation, pollution control and disaster preparedness become the planning responsibility of a single authority.
for_specific_groups.Mayors and councils: The SGA League of Mayors' President sits on the Board. SGADA may not exercise powers reserved to LGUs or encroach on their autonomy unless a law expressly provides, and needs an LGU's consent before delivering basic services there.
for_specific_groups.Interim SGADA staff: You continue in your duties with your salary and allowances until notified of a change. If displaced, you receive 1¼ months' salary for every year of service, or retirement benefits if you qualify.
for_specific_groups.Bangsamoro ministries and agencies: SGADA works in coordination with you and without duplicating your mandates. A Comprehensive Special Geographic Area Development Framework Plan will delineate functions between you, SGADA and the LGUs.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Special Geographic Area — the 8 municipalities constituted from the 63 barangays of Cotabato that joined the BARMM in the 2019 plebiscite.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: After effectivity and as SGADA's new structure, staffing and budget share take hold. The act sets no date for the master plan or the framework plan.
what_you_can_do: Ask your mayor how the municipality is represented on the SGA Board
Ask SGADA for its master plan and its Comprehensive Special Geographic Area Development Framework Plan once prepared
Read SGADA's annual report, which the Administrator submits to the Board and the Chief Minister
watch_out_for: The 2.5% share is of all Bangsamoro Government revenue collections, every year, with no ceiling. Parliament reviews it every 3 years.
The act creates the post of Administrator but does not say who appoints the Administrator or for what term.
The Chief Minister may delegate further services to SGADA pursuant to a law.
Neither the Speaker's nor the Secretary-General's signature appears on the published copy, and the approval block reads “XXX”.

key_terms_explained.Special Geographic Area (SGA): The 8 municipalities created from the barangays of Cotabato that voted to join the BARMM in 2019: Kadayangan, Kapalawan, Ligawasan, Malidegao, Nabalawag, Old Kaabakan, Pahamuddin and Tugunan (BAA 41–48).
key_terms_explained.SGA-wide services: Services with area-wide impact that cross local boundaries or cost too much for individual LGUs to provide.
key_terms_explained.Sunset clause: Section 11: the rule for winding SGADA down if the area becomes a province or political subdivision.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Safar 02, 1448 / 16 July 2026. The published copy carries no signatures and an approval block reading “XXX”.

benefits.headline: One accountable authority for services that no single SGA town can provide alone.

direct_benefits.benefit: Area-wide flood control, drainage, sewerage and irrigation planning
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Residents of the Special Geographic Area

direct_benefits.benefit: Disaster preparedness, rescue and relief coordination
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Residents of the Special Geographic Area
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Through SGADA in coordination with Bangsamoro ministries

direct_benefits.benefit: Security of tenure during transition, or separation pay of 1¼ months per year of service
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Under civil service rules, as Section 10 provides

indirect_benefits: A master plan and a framework plan delineating who does what in the area
limitations: SGADA cannot exercise LGU powers unless a law expressly provides.
Basic service delivery in a town needs that LGU's consent.

for_citizens: Pay any fees and charges SGADA lawfully imposes for its services.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no offence for individuals.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The Special Geographic Area Development Authority and its Board
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: Floods cross 3 SGA municipalities every rainy season. Planning an integrated drainage and flood-control system for all 3 is now SGADA's job, rather than 3 separate towns'.
SGADA wants to run a health programme directly in one municipality. Under Section 5 it must first coordinate with the municipality and obtain its consent.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Policy: treat the Special Geographic Area as a special development and administrative area. SGADA is a special administrative and development authority, not a political subdivision, without prejudice to LGU autonomy.

Section 2 — SGADA administers the area's affairs through planning, monitoring, coordinating and expressly provided regulatory functions, without duplicating Bangsamoro ministries and without exercising powers reserved to LGUs unless a law expressly provides.

Section 3 — SGA-wide services: development planning; flood control, drainage, sewerage and irrigation; rural, zoning and land use planning and shelter; health and sanitation, environmental protection and pollution control; public safety and disaster preparedness and relief; and other services the Chief Minister may delegate pursuant to a law.

Section 4 — The SGA Board: the SGADA Chairperson; the Minister of the Interior and Local Government; the Minister of Finance, and Budget and Management; the Bangsamoro Director General of the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority; the President of the League of Mayors in the SGA; and additional LGU and private-sector representatives as the Board determines or a law provides. The Chairperson is appointed by the Chief Minister, coterminous with the appointing authority.

Section 5 — SGADA formulates and regulates medium and long-term plans and investment programmes, manages its own programmes with Board approval, and may deliver basic services to LGUs when necessary, subject to their prior coordination and consent.
Section 6 — Functions of the Chairperson: presiding over the Board and directing policy.

Section 7 — Functions of the Administrator, head of the implementing arm: implementing Board policy, preparing the budget, appointing personnel at Salary Grade 24 and below, and submitting an annual report to the Board and the Chief Minister.

Section 8 — SGADA coordinates with LGUs, ministries and stakeholders, keeps a master plan as its development framework, and prepares a Comprehensive Special Geographic Area Development Framework Plan delineating functions.

Section 9 — Funds: the amount necessary in the annual Bangsamoro budget; a fixed annual share of 2.5% of all revenue collections of the Bangsamoro Government, reviewed by Parliament every 3 years; and fees and charges in accordance with law.

Section 10 — Transitory: interim SGADA staff continue with pay until notified; assets and liabilities pass to the expanded SGADA; displaced staff receive 1¼ months' salary per year of service or retirement benefits.

Section 11 — Sunset: if the SGA becomes a province or political subdivision, SGADA is phased out and its powers, assets, liabilities and personnel transfer under a transition plan approved by Parliament, within 2 years.
Section 12 — Repeals Sections 14, 15 and 17 to 23 of Chapter 6, Title VIII, Book VI of BAA 13 and Section 599 of BAA 49.
Sections 13–14 — Separability, and effectivity 15 days after publication in at least 2 newspapers of regional circulation.

citizen_questions.a: From the annual Bangsamoro budget, plus a fixed annual share of 2.5% of all revenue collections of the Bangsamoro Government, which Parliament reviews every 3 years. It may also impose fees and charges in accordance with law.

citizen_questions.q: Does SGADA replace the municipal governments?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 1 says it is not a political subdivision, and Section 2 bars it from exercising powers reserved to LGUs or encroaching on their autonomy unless a law expressly provides.
An SGA Board headed by a Chairperson the Chief Minister appoints, and an Administrator who runs day-to-day operations. The act does not say who appoints the Administrator.

citizen_questions.q: What happens to interim SGADA staff?
citizen_questions.a: They keep their duties, salaries and allowances until notified of a change. Displaced staff receive 1¼ months' salary for every year of service, or retirement benefits if qualified.

citizen_questions.q: What if the area becomes a province?
citizen_questions.a: SGADA is phased out under a transition plan approved by Parliament, over no more than 2 years.
No. Parliament's acts index lists this title under both numbers, but the enacted text of BAA 94 is the Pilgrimage Leave Act of 2026.
